examples.label: Set up a shared socket session (victim side)
Find sockets and check your group access
examples.command:
ps aux | grep tmux
ls -la /shareds
id

notes: A shared tmux socket owned by a privileged user and group-readable by you lets you attach to their live root session. Find the socket, confirm your group matches, attach.

recommended.note: Group membership is what grants socket access.

name: Misc - Hijack Shared tmux Session
description: A tmux session started on a group-writable socket by a privileged user can be attached by any group member - inheriting that user's shell.

defense.why_it_works: tmux sessions are accessible via UNIX socket files. If a privileged user creates a shared tmux session with a socket accessible by a group the attacker belongs to, the attacker can attach to that session and interact with it as the socket owner (e.g., root). This provides a full interactive shell as the privileged user.
defense.prerequisites: A privileged user's tmux socket file is readable/accessible by the attacker's group. Attacker is a member of that group (e.g., 'devs'). tmux installed.
defense.impact: Full interactive shell access as the socket owner (root or another privileged user). Can execute any command, read any file, and install persistent backdoors.
defense.detection: Unexpected attachment to a tmux session by a different user (tmux session logging). Auditd: tmux process opened by non-socket-owner user. who/w showing unexpected users in privileged sessions.
defense.artifacts: tmux server log (new client attached) | Auditd: open() on tmux socket by attacker | w/who output showing attacker in privileged session
defense.prevention: Never create tmux sockets in shared directories or with group permissions accessible to untrusted users. Use private socket locations with strict permissions (700). Use tmux -S only with fully trusted session participants.
defense.misconfiguration: Root creates tmux session with socket /shareds owned by root:devs with permissions 770. Attacker is a member of 'devs' group and can attach to root's session.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Insecure shared tmux session
tmux -S /shareds new -s debugsess
chown root:devs /shareds
# srwxrwx--- 1 root devs /shareds  <- devs group can attach
defense.secure_config:
# If sharing is needed, use strict permissions
tmux -S /tmp/tmux-$(id -u)-private new-session
chmod 700 /tmp/tmux-$(id -u)-private

# Never chown tmux socket to shared group
# Monitor active sessions: tmux list-sessions
